BofA Research Interpretation: Memory Stocks Trade at Only 2-3x 2027-28E P/E, the Cycle Has Not Turned Down | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsMarket AnalysisBofA Research Interpretation: ...BofA Research Interpretation: Memory Stocks Trade at Only 2-3x 2027-28E P/E, the Cycle Has Not Turned DownmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-20Last updated on 2026-10-20AbstractBank of America's October 16, 2026 report argues that memory stocks are mispriced. SK Hynix and Samsung have fallen over 50% from their June peaks, leaving them at just 2-3x 2027-28E consensus EPS—below the 4-7x seen in prior upcycles and near 1.0x 2027-28E book value, levels historically seen only at cycle bottoms. BofA maintains supercycle-level earnings forecasts: 2028 EPS declines only single digits YoY, with sales, operating profit and EPS still near 2027 peaks and record highs. So valuation prices a bottom while earnings show no downturn.

SK Hynix fell 57% from June to October, exceeding its 20-year average 51% drawdown, but in only 4 months versus the historical 15. Current DRAM ASPs are up 20-30% YoY, versus the 10-30% declines typical at bottoms. AI data center demand—LPDDR5, SOCAMM, HBM and eSSD—plus rising memory content per GPU/ASIC continues to drive growth.

Investor feedback is split: hedge funds bearish, most long-only investors bullish, with disagreement focused on cycle length rather than direction. Bear cases include neocloud borrowing costs, China 4F2 DRAM supply, falling memory per GPU, and slower AI capex. BofA rebuts each: valuations remain too low, China 4F2 impact is limited, AI backlog is large, and margins and ROIC stay high. Shareholder returns via dividends and buybacks could exceed 10% of market cap in 2027-28. BofA sees the storage TAM growing from ~$1.0tn in 2026 to over $2.0tn by 2030.

bonuses.requirements: SlowMist: Yapeswap Suffers Attack with Losses of Approximately $21,900, Attacker Gains Key Permissions with Minimal Voting PowerHomeFeedNewsSlowMist: Yapeswap Suffers Attack with Losses of Approximately $21,900, Attacker Gains Key Permissions with Minimal Voting PowerSlowMist: Yapeswap Suffers Attack with Losses of Approximately $21,900, Attacker Gains Key Permissions with Minimal Voting Power10/25 10:00According to SlowMist's monitoring, Yapeswap has been attacked, resulting in losses of approximately $21,900. The root of the incident lies in the WorkersUnion governance mechanism, which has a quorum requirement of zero. This allowed a proposal that received only about 0.000055% of voting power to transfer the feeToSetter permission of YapeFactory to the attacker. The attacker subsequently deployed a malicious Registry contract, causing latestVault() to return a forged vault address, while vaults() still listed the real vault. Deposits intended for YapePair were counted as farm assets but did not receive redeemable shares, ultimately leading to financial losses. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda hinted that consecutive rate hikes may not be necessary, but interest rates will need to rise further towards a neutral level. Committee member Junko Koeda also stated last week that the central bank should not be overly cautious regarding rate hikes. Mace News believes the most likely path is to raise rates to 1.50% in December or January, followed by an increase to 1.75% in March or April. This would continue a relatively fast pace of rate hikes every three to four months. The committee is roughly divided into four factions. Hawks Takeda Hajime and Tamura Naoki may begin pushing for the next rate hike on Friday, laying the groundwork for potential action at the December meeting. On the dovish side, Asada Tohiro and Sato Ayano have voted against recent rate hikes. In terms of data, Tokyo's October CPI is expected to show three key indicators ranging from 2.7% to 2.8%, partly reflecting the waning impact of local fiscal support. Hawks Takeda and Tamura may start pushing for the next rate hike on Friday, laying the groundwork for potential action in the December meeting. In terms of data, Tokyo's October CPI is expected to show all three key indicators between 2.7% and 2.8%, partly reflecting the waning impact of local fiscal support.
